note: Runtime dependencies allowed beyond the base, each with the reason it earned its place. A wing that wants a library adds a line here and the gate stops failing; a wing that adds one quietly does not build. Dev dependencies are listed for the record and are not gated: nothing in them reaches a visitor.

dependencies.three: The renderer. Every material of this museum is written in its shading language, which is what lets one authored wing run on both backends. Its KTX2 transcoder is the one part of it that ships as files rather than as bundle: basis_transcoder.js and basis_transcoder.wasm stand in public/basis/, copied unchanged from its own libs folder, Apache License 2.0, because the loader's worker fetches them at load.
dependencies.openseadragon: The whole plate. A painting is seen as closely as its reproduction allows through a tile pyramid, which one texture cannot carry: the National Gallery of Art's Ginevra de' Benci is 23235 x 23968 px, about 2.1 GB as a single RGBA texture. This viewer stands in the DOM over the paused canvas, so the room draws nothing while it is open, the screen bounds the memory instead of the image, and the raster passes through no post stack. Its tiles are static IIIF level-0 files in the store, so none of it runs on a server. BSD-3-Clause, imported dynamically inside the plate view, so no walk pays for its bundle.

devDependencies.playwright: the rigs: the shots, the walk, the gates
devDependencies.sharp: the tile cutter of the forge, libvips inside it; no byte of it reaches a visitor
devDependencies.vite: the dev server and the bundle
